questions.q: What is the validation set used for that distinguishes it from the training and test sets?
options: Updating the model's weights directly, just like the training set
Checking generalization after each epoch and driving decisions like when to stop training, without the model ever training on it
Only being used once at the very end to report a final score
Storing a backup copy of the training set
questions.explain: The validation set is never trained on directly; it's used after each epoch to estimate generalization and make decisions such as when to stop training or which checkpoint to keep.

questions.q: Why must the test set be touched only once, at the very end?
options: Because PyTorch limits how many times a DataLoader can be iterated
Because tuning any decision based on test-set performance makes it stop being an unbiased estimate of final performance
Because the test set is always smaller than the validation set
Because the test set cannot be loaded more than once without an error
questions.explain: The test set's value as an unbiased final estimate depends on it never influencing any training or tuning decision. Using it repeatedly to guide choices contaminates that estimate.

questions.q: Does PyTorch provide a built-in `EarlyStopping` class?
options: Yes, as part of torch.nn
Yes, as part of torch.optim
No — early stopping is a pattern you implement yourself around the training loop, tracking best validation loss and a patience counter
Yes, but only inside torchvision
questions.explain: PyTorch has no built-in EarlyStopping class. It's a hand-rolled pattern: track the best validation metric seen and a patience counter, and break out of the loop once patience is exceeded.

questions.q: In the early-stopping pattern from this lesson, what happens to `patience_counter` when validation loss improves?
options: It is incremented by 1
It is reset to 0
It is set equal to patience, stopping training immediately
It is left unchanged
questions.explain: Whenever validation loss improves on the best seen so far, the patience counter resets to 0 (and a new best checkpoint is saved); it only increments on epochs without improvement.

questions.q: Why is the checkpoint from the final epoch of a fixed-length run often not the one you should deploy?
options: The final epoch's checkpoint file is always corrupted
Validation loss commonly bottoms out and creeps back up as the model overfits, even while training loss keeps falling, so an earlier epoch's checkpoint may generalize better
PyTorch automatically deletes the final checkpoint
The final epoch never actually computes a loss
questions.explain: As training continues past the point of best generalization, validation loss often starts rising again due to overfitting even though training loss keeps improving — so the best validation checkpoint is frequently from an earlier epoch than the last one trained.
